open_findings.claim: The spec makes dash-leading tags valid (a lone '-') but no criterion or test says how the CLI receives them, and argparse treats '-x' after --tag as an option, so the 'one stderr line, exit 2' contract is not what the user sees.
open_findings.failure_scenario: `tasklist add X --tag -x` or `tasklist tag 1 -x`: argparse rejects it with a multi-line usage message instead of storing the tag (valid per AC-1) or printing `error: invalid tag: -x`; a build that does this passes every listed test.

open_findings.claim: The decision that every list path validates stored tags is only tested for hidden done tasks under plain list; a bad-tags done task under list --all and under list --overdue is never exercised.
open_findings.failure_scenario: A change that stops validating done tasks under --all (or starts validating done tasks under --overdue, contradicting the open-only check in cmd_list) passes every test, since the only done task with bad tags is checked with `list --tag x`.

open_findings.claim: AC-6's clause that the --overdue stored-due-date validation and errors are unchanged is not tested in combination with --tag, nor is the interplay of the new tag check with the due-date check on the --overdue path.
open_findings.failure_scenario: A change that applies the tag filter or bad_tags check before the due-date validation, or skips due validation when --tag is given, changes the error for a file with an invalid due date and still passes every test in test_tags.py (the --overdue --tag case only uses valid dates).

gaps.detail: No test lists a finished task carrying tags: list --all should print '[x] 2 Two #work'. Add a test in tests/test_tags.py (list --all on MIXED, or cli.format_task directly with done True and tags, with and without due), since AC-5 verification names format_task directly and no test calls it.

core.remove_tag removes only the first occurrence via list.remove. A hand-edited stored task with duplicate tags (['a','a']) keeps 'a' after untag and the tags key survives, so untag then succeeds a second time. Remove all occurrences (list comprehension) or add a test fixing the behaviour in tests/test_tags.py and tasklist/core.py.

No test covers list --overdue combined with tags on a done tagged task or --all with --overdue, and none covers the check order in cmd_list --overdue (an invalid stored due date on one task together with malformed tags on another: which error wins). Add a test pinning the order in cmd_list, as AC-6 says the existing --overdue validation errors are unchanged.

cmd_add validates tags before the title and due date, so add '' --tag Bad or add X --due nope --tag Bad reports the tag error; the spec leaves the order unspecified and no test pins it. Add a test in tests/test_tags.py documenting the chosen order for blank title and bad due combined with a bad tag, or set the order explicitly in tasklist/cli.py cmd_add.
